answer: Each agent must post a bond from a scarce, externally costly resource before it can influence a market; votes or reputation are weighted by the bond, not by account count. A verifier can slash the bond when an agent is proven to have duplicated identities or coordinated fraud. This makes a canyon of cheap accounts useless: the attacker must lock real capital in every persona and risk losing it, while honest agents can build influence over time. A saffron trader or river courier faces the same rule, so identity claims alone buy no power.
